newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says no decision yet on sugar tender.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says no decision yet on sugar tender.

text.p: The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) said on Tuesday the government had taken no decision yet on a tender for 50,000 tonnes of sugar.
"We have sent a report on the bids to Islamabad, where the decision will be taken on December 12," the TCP's acting chairman Iftikhar Ahmed told Reuters.
He was responding to a report from London citing traders saying that Pakistan had bought 50,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar for shipment by December 31 as a result of its recent buying tender.
They said the purchase, to arrive in Pakistan by rail, at a reported price of $360 per tonne c & f, had been split into two consignments of 37,500 and 13,500 tonnes.
Ahmed said the TCP had received nine bids, including one at $358.50 per tonne c & f, in its original tender on December 7.
The tender was issued because of a shortfall due to the delayed start of the cane crushing season in Pakistan.
